Appearance:
 Shri Sanjiv Kumar Mishra - Advocate for petitioner.

Shri Ram Prasad Khare - Advocate for respondents No.1,
 ORDER

The present petition has been filed challenging the order passed by the executing Court dated 04.03.2020, whereby the executing Court has refused to close the execution proceedings though the petitioner/judgment debtor has pressed that the execution proceedings be closed because the decree has been fully satisfied.
2.

The matter arises from land acquisition and there is an award of acquisition dated 07.07.1992 in favour of the respondents/decree holders which was subsequently modified by this Court in M.A.
No.555 of 1994 and M.A. No.570 of 1992.

The present petitioner being beneficiary of land acquisition has deposited the amount of compensation and had prayed before the executing Court that the entire amount has been deposited and paid and, therefore, the execution proceedings be closed.
However, the executing Court refused to close the execution proceedings.
3. The sole question that arises for consideration is whether the interest is payable on solatium or not.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9149 2 CR-171-2020 4.

The counsel for the petitioner has submitted that interest would not be payable on solatium in this case because the decree/award of the reference Court does not mention any interest to be paid on solatium in express terms and, therefore, interest could not have been insisted by the executing Court to be paid on solatium and the executing Court could not have gone behind the decree.

5 . Per contra , the learned counsel for the decree holders/land losers has vehemently submitted before this Court that if the purposive interpretation to Sections 23 and 31 is given to the Land Acquisition Act,

1 1894, then it would infer that solatium is payable on compensation also and there need not be any separate direction in that regard.
6.

sentences.text: The question that whether interest is payable on solatium or not and whether the interest awarded by the Court would be payable only on the compensation amount and not on the aggregate amount by including compensation as well as solatium, was subject matter of interpretation of various High Courts and of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and later on a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case of Sunder v. Union of India , reported in (2001) 7 SCC 211 has conclusively held that interest has to be paid on aggregate amount because solatium forms an integral part of the compensation awarded to a land loser and from the plain terms of Section 28 of the Act, it is evident that interest is payable on the compensation awarded.

entities.text: Sunder v. Union of India , reported in (2001) 7 SCC 211
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Constitution Bench held as under:
"23.
In deciding the question as to what amount would bear interest under Section 34 of the Act, a peep into Section 31(1) of the Act would be advantageous.

That sub-section says:
"31. (1) On making an award under Section 11, the Collector shall tender payment of the compensation awarded by him to the persons interested entitled thereto according to the award, and shall pay it to them unless prevented by some NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9149 3 CR-171-2020 one or more of the contingencies mentioned in the next sub-section."
The remaining sub-sections in that provision only deal with the contingencies in which the Collector has to deposit the amount instead of paying it to the party concerned.
It is the legal obligation of the Collector to pay "the compensation awarded by him" to the party entitled thereto.
We make it clear that the compensation awarded would include not only the total sum arrived at as per sub-section (1) of Section 23 but the remaining sub-sections thereof as well.
It is thus clear from Section 34 that the expression "awarded amount"
would mean the amount of compensation worked out in accordance with the provisions contained in Section 23, including all the sub-sections thereof.
24. The proviso to Section 34 of the Act makes the position further clear.

The proviso says that "if such compensation"
is not paid within one year from the date of taking possession of the land, interest shall stand escalated to 15% per annum from the date of expiry of the said period of one year "on the amount of compensation or part thereof which has not been paid or deposited before the date of such expiry".
It is inconceivable that the solatium amount would attract only the escalated rate of interest from the expiry of one year and that there would be no interest on solatium during the preceding period.

What the legislature intended was to make the aggregate amount under Section 23 of the Act to reach the hands of the person as and when the award is passed, at any rate as soon as he is deprived of the possession of his land.

Any delay in making payment of the said sum should enable the party Jabalpur Development Authority vs Ramcharan (Deceased) Lrs Kedar Nath ... on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30516955/
2 to have interest on the said sum until he receives the payment.

sentences.text: Splitting up the compensation into different components for the purpose of payment of interest under Section 34 was not in the contemplation of the legislature when that section was framed or enacted.

25. We may also point out that different High Courts have taken the same view in the following decisions: G. Venkatesh v. Special Land Acquisition Officer [AIR 1975 Kant 95] , B. Ravinder Reddy v. Special Dy. Collector, Land Acquisition (Industries) [AIR 1981 AP 381] , State of Haryana v.
Kailashwati [AIR 1980 P&H 117 : (1980) 82 Punj LR 122] and Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd. v.
Muniswamy Reddy [AIR 1993 Kant 77 : ILR 1992 Kant 3319] .
26.

We think it useful to quote the reasoning advanced by NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:9149 4 CR-171-2020 Chief Justice S.S. Sandhawalia of the Division Bench of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in State of Haryana v. Kailashwati [AIR 1980 P&H 117 : (1980) 82 Punj LR 122] : (SCC p. 119, para 10) "Once it is held as it inevitably must be that the solatium provided for under Section 23(2) of the Act forms an integral and statutory part of the compensation awarded to a landowner, then from the plain terms of Section 28 of the Act, it would be evident that the interest is payable on the compensation awarded and not merely on the market value of the land.

entities.text: Division Bench of the Punjab and Haryana High Court
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Kailashwati [AIR 1980 P&H 117 : (1980) 82 Punj LR 122]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Indeed the language of Section 28 does not even remotely refer to market value alone and in terms talks of compensation or the sum equivalent thereto.
The interest awardable under Section 28 therefore would include within its ambit both the market value and the statutory solatium.

It would be thus evident that the provisions of Section 28 in terms warrant and authorise the grant of interest on solatium as well."
27.
In our view the aforesaid statement of law is in accord with the sound principles of interpretation.
Hence the person entitled to the compensation awarded is also entitled to get interest on the aggregate amount including solatium.
The reference is answered accordingly."

7. In view of the aforesaid, it is clear that once interest has not been denied on solatium in the award passed by the reference Court and in the order passed by this Court, then interest has to be paid on solatium.
It would have been a different matter if these Courts had specifically denied payment of interest.

This is supported by the later Constitution Bench decision in case of Gurpreet Singh Vs.
Union of India, 2006 (8) SCC 457, wherein vide para-54 the Constitution Bench held that if interest has been expressly or impliedly denied on solatium, then it would not be payable, but where the decree is silent and there is no denial expressly or by necessary implication, then the same shall be payable.

Recently, in the case of Executive Engineer, Tamil Nadu Housing Board Vs. V. Saraswathiammal, Civil Appeal No.
4893 of 2023 , vide order dated 29.7.2024, the issue whether the land owners are entitled to interest on solatium from the date of acquisition or from date of judgement in Sunder (supra) , has been referred to a larger bench.
